title: Separate Output from Failure
concept: Return observable stdout, stderr and exit status

writing.summary: Return observable stdout, stderr and exit status.
writing.rule: Data goes to stdout; a failure has stderr context and a nonzero status.
writing.explanation:
Automation observes a program through more than its printed text. A machine may consume stdout as data and use the exit status to decide whether the next stage may run. Putting an error into stdout while returning success makes a broken command look like a valid empty result.

Use status 0 for a successful task count and 2 for a usage or input error in this CLI contract. Error text belongs on stderr and ends in a newline. Do not add a success banner to machine-readable stdout. A program that crashes or fails compilation is different from a deliberate domain error; retain that distinction when diagnosing the terminal result. The finite lab models the three outputs so tests can assert them separately; the companion uses println, eprintln and process::exit at its actual boundary.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Run a valid and an invalid companion CLI invocation and compare output, error stream and exit result.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: The worked implementation exercises return observable stdout, stderr and exit status. Its tests demonstrate the stated finite contract.
writing.task: Return stdout, stderr and exit code. Success emits COUNT followed by newline only on stdout with 0; errors emit error: MESSAGE followed by newline only on stderr with 2. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: A command prints an error but exits with status 0. What is wrong for automation?
answers: The command reports success through its status
Any text on stderr automatically changes the exit status
writing.feedback: Writing stderr does not itself set a nonzero process exit status.
